data: I do wish the true ending was a little more satisfying and rewarding
Gameplay is great and story is amazing
Love this game -- very challenging and immersive
This instant classic offers an incredible amount of content and secrets to discover and is a must-play for anyone who enjoys a well-crafted game
the art style is unique and amazing and the atmosphere is great 10 / 10 game
After a while, the game becomes repetitive, boring and frustrating
Gameplay is boring, the story is too basic and the puzzles are too complicated
sadly, all of this is buried under a cavalcade of utterly trite RNG mechanics that do nothing
In Blue Prince, the "content" is stretched so thin and inaccessible that to me it no longer becomes worthwhile to pursue
After this you'll spend hours and hours of your life trying to get the RNG necessary to actually hit the objectives and beat the game
once you enter the endgame and the light stats shining on where you are and what you are doing the game becomes too RNG dependent
Gameplay is boring, the story is too basic and the puzzles are too complicated
it doesn't give me any indication on what I'm supposed to be writing down in my pages of notes
Which is a shame, because the concept, story, worldbuilding, atmosphere, and artstyle of the game are pretty good
I guess then if you have even a slight aversion to roguelike gameplay, I can't recommend this game
-7 for poor gameplay and grueling game design
I could not tell you even in the slightest how to do that after 30 minutes of gameplay

It's fun for a while, but frankly, it's not just random, it's too damn random, and a lot of things you need to do depend on perfect draws, and mutually exclusive with lots of other things you need to do.

... In other words... Imagine playing solitaire, only where you have not 8 piles, but just 2 (and that doesn't mean you get 6 empty spots, you don't -- it's 2 piles total). It's THAT kind of perfect draw dependent.
Looks like a great game. But I won't (and can't) experience it until an official Chinese localization is released, since my English level isn't good enough to fully enjoy it.

i genuinely hate this game. this is one of the most miserable experiences ive had playing this game. genuinely it gives me so much hope before deciding to kill me, my family, my dog, then sell all of our organs to china at a price too cheap for organs. its like edging only if before she lets me cum she decides to chop off my dick. i hate this game so much for what its put me through. 10/10 im gonna 100% it

One of the greatest puzzle games you'll ever play. It's part roguelite, but that's not really the meat of the game. This is a puzzle game.

The difficulty curve starts relatively flat and eventually bends upwards, and then upwards sharply, and then...seemingly never ends. That's not entirely true - it does have an ending, but you may find the game becomes so incredibly difficult that you never see the ending that the game dangles in front of you for the entire of your time with it.

Expect to have to take notes (not from the very beginning, but eventually), and even if you hate the idea of taking notes for a game, expect this game to make you come to love it.

This game has arguably one of the greatest stories, secreted away so incredibly well, that I've ever seen in a game.

Im going to say that this is an extremely fun and frustrating puzzle game... But it's frustrating in all the right ways. Puzzles are difficult and very very intricate on some occasions. Use a notebook and make notes or take screen shots as you continue building and rebuilding this mansion to finally solve this well thought out bizarre clue like sandbox style puzzle. Love it. Can play at your own pace.

I'll admit I am not a fan of puzzle games with too much RNG and have to try everything again from the start to solve the knot. I've taken a pause after 10 hours of Blue Prince (6 hours actually because I forgot to turn off my monitor) because the RNG of room/item spawn really bothers me. At the time of this comment, I just finished getting the basement key and too lazy to continue the game.

But objectively, Blue Prince is a good game. Its mechanics are very refreshing among the puzzle game genres and have an exceptional storytelling, balance and details. I love that every room will reveal a bit of story behind the estate, the protagonist and the characters in the game. Every room have its own unique atmosphere and use. So if you don't mind the repetition of a roguelike game and the slow pace of it, you will have tons of things to explore in Mt. Holly Estate, bit by bit each day. Definitely a game that every puzzle lover should try.

I'll come back to the game later. Still curious for what will happen in room 46 :)
The game mechanics are really interesting and the mysteries are genuinely intriguing, but to solve the mysteries you have to rely so much on RNG and it just takes forever to advance.

10/10 game, would fall into this rabbit hole again.
Jokes aside, if you are into puzzle games, buy this.

While I enjoy a good puzzle but Blue Prince doesn't respect your time , you're frequently dealing with a bad house layout, rooms that you need and don't show up, running out of keys/gems/steps and the parlor game that becomes longer and longer every time you solve it.

I want to like the game more but every time I want to draft a parlor for gems I'm frustrated by the amount of time it takes to deal with it, or the amount of times my house ends up like a tiny shack because there's no way to reroll bad layouts without gaining some dice, plus having to go out and do something at the start of every run at a certain point of the game, having a metal detector wastes your time by having you look around a room for keys and coins.

Not to mention having entire long runs in which you accomplish nothing because the rooms that you wanted to do things in didn't spawn at all...

Yeah, the game mechanic with the roguelike+puzzle combination is certainly novel, and refreshing at first. But very soon the random element is just so frustrating. You have the solution for some puzzle, and then it takes you several runs just to pray the RNG gives you the right rooms and items to actually solve it to make progress. 
I played for around 6 hours, I essentially already know how to get to the end credits - median play time to actually get there is 17 hours, i.e. I'd have another 11 hours of grinding the RNG? No thank you. 
My take-away: Puzzles and RNG don't mix in a satisfying way...

Sad to see so many negative reviews from people dropping this game during its opening hours. I understand some of the frustrations, but I promise this is a game that rewards the effort you put in and delivers some great moments.

I have reached the credits but still have many more hours to spend solving the major mysteries of the game. I can't speak to the quality of the content to come, but the game is well worth the money- even if what I have played to this point were all there was.

This game is beautiful, and wonderfully polished.

With that said, the core mechanic of the game gets in the way of the puzzles. You may find a puzzle room one day, and the clues for the puzzle on other days and then you're sat there waiting for the puzzle room to reappear. Another reviewer said it best (paraphrasing): this game doesn't respect my time.

Is player skill the deciding factor in this game? That is, given a new game; can a skilled player consistently beat the game? I don't know, but I doubt it.

I *really* want to like this game. But the RNG just gets in the way of it.

I'm in deep. The game feels like an actual mystery that you're actually solving by actually finding actual clues (actually). The pacing feels pretty nice so far in terms of progressing through the game. I have a notebook filled with notes and I've taken lots of screenshots. If you enjoy a challenging puzzle game where you really need to think, you should try this game!

What can I say after 550 hours? It is simply a masterpiece. Not only is it one of the best puzzle games I've ever played, rivalled only by The Witness, it is also one of the best games I've ever played, full stop. How many times did I find myself at a dead end, only to pour over my notes and realize a clue has been staring me in the face all along? How many times did I think to myself "I think I'm finally closing in on the end", only to find that there was so much more left to uncover? Despite never seeing another soul, the world feels rich and historied. I spent three months wandering these halls by myself, and yet I never really felt alone. In my 33 years of gaming, this is only the fourth game to ever bring me to tears. The only regret I leave behind is that I can never again play it for the first time. If you're reading this and contemplating your first playthrough, I have but one piece of advice for you: take your time. Rush nothing, and savor the challenges. And when it is finally over, don't forget to smile.
-Ovinn Nevarei
I have a notebook to keep track of things for this game and I've just hit 3 whole ass pages of notes. Every time I open up the book I feel like I'm going insane. 10/10

For people who enjoy exploration and puzzles in their games, this game is one of the best ever made.
This plays sort of like a time loop, or a non-combative puzzle-filled rogue-lite, of the kind that wants you to learn and improve each and every iteration - and there are tons of things to learn and improve in this game.

This is one of my favorite games ever now, and it's recommended beyond words. This is almost Outer Wilds-tier of experience, and that game IMO is the best one ever made.

One thing though - don't come into it in the mindset that "this run I will solve mystery X no matter what" because rooms and items are drawn randomly and you just might not be able to solve the mystery your mind locked on whenever you feel like it. Always keep an open mind and open eyes - there are tons of things to discover and solve, and even if you won't solve said mystery X this very next run, you'll solve it in the future.

This is addictive and you become completely obsessed with it. Best game I've ever played. The way it reveals information as you go keeps you coming back for more. Achievements feel well earned. Fascinating, intriguing, brilliant!

I love. This Game. So. Freaking. Much. I am literally over 20 hours in, and I'm 100% certain I haven't even scratched the tip of the iceberg. It's a puzzle wrapped in a puzzle and then another layered on top of it. I. LOVE. IT. Also, I really like how everything kinda looks like it's made out of cardboard. I don't know if that's a part of the lore or if it's a stylistic choice, but either way I really dig it.

Blue Prince offers a wonderful marriage of puzzle and roguelite design elements rewarding careful observation, patience and exploration through every door of a mysterious and capricious manor. Keep a notepad handy and refrain from Googling puzzle solutions for the best experience; yes, that bishop chess piece in the chapel is worth remembering. Hundreds of tiny details will turn over in your noggin long after you call it a day both in and out of game. Then, when you least expect, a new clue will fire off a surge of dopamine and inch you ever closer to finding Room 46. 200 hours in and while I've achieved many of Blue Prince's primary objectives, there are dozens of puzzles, bits of lore and surprises left to uncover. Curiosity may yet keep me opening Mt. Holly doors for another 200 hours more. 10/10.

Drafting your target room is not as hard as the other comments mentioned if you have a sound strategy, I never had to look for a room or a combination of rooms for more than two days in a row. Very nice combo of roguelike and puzzles, rewarding to find room 46. However after room 46 the goal is less clear and makes me less motivated. post-46 puzzles are hard and I had to look up many of them. Also there's no satisfying ending and the developers decided to leave it with quote 'does it never end?'... Though still a very decent game and I strongly recommend it.
It is CRIMINAL how underrated this game is. Everything, every object, every line of text is part of an interconnecting puzzle system. Easily the BEST puzzle game ever made. 10/10
This game's basically like a Hydra; for every puzzle you solve, another two takes its place. How deep does this go?

The RNG in the game makes me feel like I’m wasting my time instead of just solving puzzles and enjoying the gameplay. The roguelike element doesn’t work for me in this game... maybe it would if a day somehow lasted three times less, allowing for quicker trial and error. Right now, I have a list of multiple possible things that could progress the game, but I’m just not getting the right room and item combinations to make any of them happen. I might finish it, but I’m not recommending this even at a discount.

This is the best puzzle game i've ever played. It seemingly never ends, and constantly surprises me.

Thats all cool, but what i really want to talk about is the atmosphere and story of this game (obviously avoiding spoilers)

There is a profound loneliness and slightly creepy atmosphere suffused into the game, and it makes the exploration feel so real? I feel like i'm actually exploring some weird old building that I don't understand, and I genuinely feel in line with the character. Discovering mismatched details about the lore, and the satisfaction that came with realizing "oh my god, this is who that is!" was always a pleasant experience. Not to mention every answer happened to be another clue towards something I didn't know about yet, branching the game in yet another new direction. The message of the story to the player character, and especially who its from, feels so profound to the character even if the player might not care.

In terms of the gameplay itself, I recommend any new player to keep their options open. Like any roguelike, going for a specific "build" is a recipe for failure- don't pass up good options just because they don't fit the "build" or "goal". Be flexible, and you'll have a better time.

Good game, 10/10 up until the deep post-game.
Truly my favourite game for 2025. I've been craving puzzle games like this with rich rich world building. Highly reccomend, just don't watch too much before getting into it!

Probably a great one if you liked Point and Click games, but it's not for me. Having to write down obscure clues, be at mercy of RNG and walk very slowly made me quite bored after a couple of hours. I hope there are updates to address the slow walking and animations, and some kind of progression so it's less RNG based. Then I'd give it another try.

Much like Balatro in 2024, Dredge in 2023, and other indie darlings in previous years, Blue Prince comes out of the gate as a strong contender for my personal game of the year. The main draw of Blue Prince is how well the game includes a strong central puzzle (and a magnitude of other puzzles varying in complexity) into the classic "one more run" roguelite formula. You'll be completely tunnel visioned on solving the main puzzle of the game and then another puzzle snakes it way into your brain. The use of drafting rooms to create your own maze inside Mt. Holly is ingenious and so seamlessly makes for an engaging gameplay loop, I'm surprised it hasn't been done before. The game is quite RNG heavy, as are all roguelites, and while I understand how thay can be frustrating to some, I see it as a part of the genre. Games that handle RNG well still allow you to find something new or learn pertinent information relevant to future runs and Blue Prince does succeed at this in my opinion.

If you want to get in early on a potential GOTY candidate, pull the trigger now to avoid as many spoilers as possible

I was unhesitatingly going to give this game a recommendation, but I'm still trying to finish it and it has really pissed me off. The best way to play this game is to have a friend who has already finished it whom you can ask questions of. People say they finished it in 90 hours, but clearly that's not been the case for me. I don't like getting hints, but you WILL HAVE TO GET HINTS for this. The *main* problem is, as you get later into the game, it gets harder and harder to understand what you're supposed to do. You have to make some leaps of logic - now those leaps may be clued to you later - but you won't know that. Did you miss something? You don't know. The ideal player of this game is an archaeologist who is willing to map every inch of every room. And you'll have time to, cause you'll be drafting them over and over and over. You can't just "try something". You have to beat the RNG to get the chance to try something. And then you'll be wrong. You get the idea.

I want to love this game. I do love parts of this game; the visual style, the atmosphere, the polish. Everything else is crap, though. The RNG that so many other reviewers denounce is exactly what kills this game. In Blue Prince, you aren't completing puzzles to progress - you are completing puzzles usually only once, and then relying on drafting the right room to make a run work. Your runs fail based on RNG early on, and you think "Okay, I just got unlucky. I'll try again and maybe luck will be on my side!" Luck is never on your side. There is nothing to learn that meaningfully offsets the potential for RNG to stop a run dead in its tracks. You do not discover more about the mansion as the game progresses (unless you count bits of lore), you simply end up playing a more braindead version of the game, as you're just speedrunning, hoping for the right set of rooms to make a viable run. Don't draft the right rooms? Call it a day, start over. It's so frustrating that this game, with so much thought and style put into it, falls flat on its face in the mid to late game. Don't waste your money.

It's good but I can't recommend it. Without giving any spoilers - The puzzles are too disconnected from the reward, the random element makes it a grind to even try to solve them. I've had my fun with it, but it's not a positive experience in the end and I'll not know rest of the story.

Inspiringly beautiful and so much deeper than I expected. Probably the best puzzle game I've played to date. Once I got to grips with just how smart most of the puzzle design is I found almost every discovery on my own. Keeping a notebook handy is definitely a must. Each time I started writing down the clues and puzzles I'd eventually reach a point where it all fell into place as if I was in the midst of some kind of treasure-hunt movie. I seriously gasped at moments, shocked by revelations of information that was hiding in plain sight in a way that was neither obvious nor reminiscent of early point-and-click moon logic. Just right.

There were a few moments where I gave up on something a little too hard to figure out, only to feel a little dumb for looking it up. One or two of these moments felt a little like a dirty trick, but I'm willing to forgive a couple of tricky puzzles for the sheer amount of brilliant ones within.

In short, it'll take time and effort, but if you're willing to immerse yourself in these kinds of puzzles you're going to love this game.
this game is too rng heavy, most of the time it just feels like you're on auto pilot with the lack of items each run gives you.

A great game to play when you want so quiet downtime. Story telling is subtle yet effective as you discover much of it while searching for ways to progress in the game. There's a nice amount of hidden complexity and unexpected mechanics that keep the experience fun slowly evolving.

Overall fun puzzle game
Blend of rogue lite rng with walking sim puzzling feels fresh take on the genre, but also brings its own frustrations
Game has lots of mysteries to solve, though keeping your own notes or/and using a guide is paramount
would recommend for patient puzzle solvers up for a challenge
One of the few games where the tutorial is its own game. 100/10 definitely recommend.

If you cross Myst, Magic the Gathering, and a book of Dad Jokes, you get Blue Prince. And if you love all three then be warned, this game is CRACK. I beat the first main objective on day 30-something (day 3 of playing, haha) and I'm on day 90-something now.

After having sat on this for a while, i think my conclusion is that this is game is terrible in unique enough ways that its worthwhile to see. Obviously don't play it if you're trying to have fun or whatever, but its a very neat exploration to the somewhat unique experience resulting from having several layers overlaid with basically no connection between them.

This game has a really neat vibe to it, but it just feels like it has a single story to tell and the game mechanics stretch that out in a weird and frustrating way. I kept at it longer than I should have (too late for a refund) hoping to find the hook that brought me back, but the only thing that kept me playing was trying to find out why so many folks rated it so high.

It is a beautiful game. It's reminiscent of Myst with a completely incomprehensible restart mechanic.

I'm not sure I can see this having any replayability after the story is solved, and I might be selling it short by not finishing the game, but the charm wore off before finishing the story.

I can't recommend at full price, maybe with a pretty steep discount.

Very interesting and engaging. I like exploration games with puzzles. The early puzzles are pretty easy, but I expect them to get harder. So far fun without the frustration of some exploration/puzzle games.

A game that could have been great ruined by annoying RNG. The mystery is compelling yes, but not so much that I want to suffer through re-roll after re-roll. I recommend watching a lore video or something instead of playing this.

Everything in this game is too goddam slow! The walk speed, the animations, the time it takes to restart a run, it's all so grindingly, frustratingly slow! Especially for a rogue-lite where trying and failing multiple runs is the core gameplay loop. I don't know if I'll be able to finish it at this point, which is a review in and of itself. The accessibility options are nice, but there needs to be one called "respect my time" that speeds everything up. FFS.

My favorite game of the year, Blue Prince is game with unique mechanics, challenging puzzles, and never-ending mysteries to unravel. Logic, wordplay, and observational puzzles abound, scattered about an ever-changing mansion you build as you explore. Strategy, note-taking, and persistence are required, but they're well-rewarded. From finally finding Room 46 to solving a puzzle that's tormented you and being rewarded with a whole new mystery thread to explore, to drafting exactly the right room at the right time, the game provides a sense of earned achievements that keeps you coming back for more.

Really fun rogue-like that is an early contender for GotY.
I was hesitant to play this because I feared the puzzles making a fool of me, but there are plenty of ways to solve each and you can approach them from a variety of ways.
Cell shaded animations are beautiful, music is haunting and thematic, game play is simple but be prepared with a notebook and lots of screenshots.

9.5/10
A nice collection of puzzles and overarching mystery that keeps things fresh and encourages you to try one more time.

Initially, this game is pretty interesting and engaging with its focus on puzzles and discovery. Solving these puzzles can be genuinely enjoyable, initially. However, the core gameplay loop quickly devolves into a significant grind. Progressing towards the later stages, particularly reaching the antechamber, feels overwhelmingly reliant on random chance rather than strategic choices.

After numerous runs (easily 30-40+ days in-game), the puzzles, despite their initial appeal, become repetitive and feel more like obstacles than engaging content. The joy of uncovering secrets diminishes with each iteration. This repetitive nature, coupled with the seemingly high degree of RNG in progression, leads to a feeling of boredom and disillusionment.

While I appreciate the puzzle design and the potential for deeper exploration, the excessive grind and reliance on luck significantly hinder the overall enjoyment. The prospect of countless more repetitive runs just to experience the remaining content has become unappealing. Ultimately, the core mechanic's grindy nature overshadows the otherwise interesting puzzle elements, making it difficult to recommend for players who value consistent progress and less reliance on random outcomes.

Wow, truly a masterpiece.
Who could have imagine a house building rogue like would be so much fun?
Uncovering all the lore, all the extra rooms, and formulating a strategy through such a clever gameplay loop is such a joy. Sometimes it can be frustrating to watch a really good run turn bad in two unlucky draws of dead ends, but you just restart and go again.
Be ready with a notepad, don't get too attached to each run, and accept that you will likely find Room 46 before you finish everything else. There are still secrets I'm sure I don't know that I don't know.
If you like exploration puzzles, deep lore, and amazing atmospheres, pick this one up.

Blue Prince is an excellent combination of roguelite and puzzle game. I really enjoyed beating this game and I highly recommend it. As it is a roguelite it leads to some puzzles being RNG dependent but I enjoyed playing the actual roguelite so this was only a small issue for me. Both the roguelite strategy game and the puzzles were really well made

I hate this game.
I hate it so much that I'm writing this review.
At first it was nice and interesting - almost every run you uncover something new. But after day 20 I spent another 20 praying for good random. I would start the run, draft rooms, find out that I dont have neccesary rooms (yes, you need several) or I do have them but in the wrong places (yes, you must place them correctly), and I start over. And again. And again. And again... And finally - after 20 or something runs - it happened! I drafted all needed rooms to get to antechamber... to find out that I need another one that I dont have! So this run was also useless! Yes, it gave me another piece of the puzzle - that I need yet another room in this random!
So the thing that pisses me off and makes me Not recommend this game is that it's not a puzzle game - you don't win here with your wits or brain or memory or anythinh - you just wait for perfect run where all the pieces magically fall in places.

I really want to like this game because it has everything that I like about games. However, I think the roguelike elements do this game a disservice because getting the rooms you need is entirely random and I cant find a way to stack the deck in my favor like how other roguelikes operate. Early game is very fun because your finding clues, solving puzzles and finding out about the lore. But after playing 10 hours it starts to slow down to a grinding halt. No new rooms, No additional buffs, clues are more obscure and when you do finally solve a puzzle, its already been hours. This game has so much potential and I hope I can come back and finish it, but its just too boring right now.

The most addictive game I've played since I was a kid playing Sonic The Hedgehog 3. I've never played anything like it and was never into these types of games before. I've got hundreds of hours across multiple platforms. Room 46 is just the beginning and it's an amazingly immersive play. Glad i've got it on my mac now so I can take it anywhere.

tldr.text: Very Positive (86%): 28% of reviews praise the story and characters, the game's biggest draw.
The main complaint is the repetitive content and grind, which some players find boring and frustrating.

details.text: Recent reviews are slightly less positive at 82%, while complaints about the grind and story are unchanged.
Players with the least playtime are far less positive than veterans, at 40% against 94% for the longest-playing group.
